title: Concept ​
use_cases: Use when identifying the four Throughline Perspectives of a new story idea
Use when translating a fuzzy premise into a workable narrative map before drafting
Use when seeking to formalize explicit structural choices for a narrative
Configure when the current story premise feels under-specified or lacks direction
content:
Story Decoder is an early-stage Storyform discovery tool. It identifies the four Throughline Perspectives, proposes key audience dynamics, and translates your premise into a workable narrative map.

Plain-language translation: Story Decoder helps you see what kind of argument your story is already trying to make before you start drafting scenes.

Most story ideas feel clear in your head but fuzzy on the page. Story Decoder turns that fuzzy idea into explicit structural choices so you can write with direction instead of guessing.

When the four Throughline Perspectives and core dynamics are visible, you can decide what to draft first, what to revise, and where your current premise is under-specified.
